scope.objective: Reduce repeated game-wide work and clarify system ownership while preserving the playable game's physical logistics and timing contracts.
scope.implementation_authorization: The user authorized proceeding with the overhaul after reviewing the investigation. Implement and validate bounded slices against the protected contracts; proposed phases remain incomplete until their exit conditions are evidenced.
scope.inventory: overhaul_inventory.json preserves the original 166-script audit; its current_source_status records drift. system_map.json inventories current code, including new read characterization fixtures.
scope.review_depth: Whole-project structural inventory plus direct reading of the central clock, settlement, command, mutation, safety, cancellation and completion paths cited below. This is not a claim that every implementation-derived purpose or every gameplay scenario has been independently verified.
scope.execution: Original investigation was documentation-only. The subsequent first P00/P01 slice executed native pre-change characterization captures and the isolated GdUnit4 suite; bounded results and the remaining live failure are recorded in evidence/overhaul_read_slice.json. Subsequent E07 adds native UI/construction acceptance coverage and longer targeted performance checks without changing gameplay implementations.
scope.freshness: baseline_source_hashes and existing anchors retain the original source epoch. current_source_anchors and overhaul_inventory.current_source_status identify deliberate changes; consult the living map and actual source before later migrations.

recommendation.direction: Retire live world-wide advance_time/settlement through independently progressing persistent logistics/battlefield owners, scoped committed events and owned local timed work. Preserve authoritative physical state and explicit causal handoffs; a shared world clock is not required.
recommendation.clock: E14 supersedes the shared-clock requirement. Both domains progress while hidden; retain current Pause/1x/2x user intent as the default local timing policy. Define local tie order and transfer causality without aligning timestamps. Native Timer/_physics_process mechanisms are preferred where suitable and verified; do not recreate all-service polling.
recommendation.godot_usage: Use scene-owned Nodes for lifecycle/input/presentation, signals for notifications and Timer for suitable local timed behavior. Keep large data models as data; converting every record/job/state into a Node is not a prerequisite for correct Godot use.
recommendation.first_behavioral_pilot: Military leader eligibility and HQ automatic assignment/issue, after source-level read reductions and characterization tests.
recommendation.current_next_slice: Resolve measured whole-frame budget failures before accepting further overhaul slices: profile inside opening-policy/physical admission and planning-owner calls, then bound pure preparation and fresh atomic commits without dropping simulation work, weakening checks or changing rates. Continue scoped event/local-owner migration only with 16.67 ms whole-frame evidence, correctness, liveness and custody gates.
avoid: A simultaneous replacement of all services, UI, ledger and movement.
A Timer per entity or a slower Timer that still scans the entire world.
Deferring all signals indiscriminately, including contact damage and wreck resolution.
A second authoritative inventory, duplicated scheduler ownership, or a global untyped event bus.
Treating low function counts, syntax checks or the menu sweep as complete correctness evidence.
Changing movement speed, recipe costs, capacities, default opening or observation cadence to hide performance problems.
Adding editor addons, threads, ECS, C# migration or rendering-server code before measurements justify them.

current_execution_order.description: Order is observable and must be characterized before moving work between callbacks.
within_advance: Scan service, actor and job boundaries for the next endpoint.
Accrue eligible production/training/construction work using the interval's staffing/access state.
Advance physical actors and several service motions; synchronous movement callbacks can apply contact consequences.
Advance ledger and rear clocks, then remaining vehicle-combat/recovery/receiving work.
Run global settlement again and emit state/time notifications.
current_execution_order.settle_behavior: A settlement invocation scans many services, actors and stores; if any service changes state, another global pass can occur. The 1000-iteration loop is a convergence limit, not evidence that every frame performs 1000 passes.
current_execution_order.command_behavior: Some domain setters call rear._settle directly; BaseDemo._result can also call simulation.after_command, which invalidates planning and performs zero-time settlement. A result's ok flag alone is not a reliable mutation/revision contract.

E01.window: Completed engine second 4 in a bounded 1x Build observation.
E01.limits: One recorded opening window with stack instrumentation; not a CPU profile, whole-game benchmark, or proof every repeat is redundant.
E01.availability: Raw logs are local ignored artifacts, not assumed present in a fresh checkout; the plan preserves the reported measurements and their limits.

E02.observations: The same direct Build refresh probe dropped from 1251 to 1 full inspections and from 41.253 to 1.111 ms after narrow reads.
E02.limits: Individual measurements, not a statistical benchmark. Protect this already-achieved behavior.

E03.observations: The formal sweep stopped during Open Build observation on a 162.232 ms frame against a 100 ms budget, before later menus were certified.
E03.limits: A frame interval includes pacing/scheduling and does not attribute CPU time to the last clicked handler.
E03.availability: Raw logs are local ignored artifacts, not assumed present in a fresh checkout; the plan preserves the reported measurements and their limits.

E04.observations: Original 166-script static audit. Its source hashes and candidate locations are preserved as history; current_source_status identifies changed/added files. Counts are static review locations, not current runtime frequencies or proof of redundant work.

E05.observations: Caller grouping has guards for two different cross-file origins, real-second boundaries and counters-only mode. The game regression coverage remains bounded as documented in performance_testing.md.

E06.observations: All ten focused guards passed; all 13 pre-change state hashes match. Repeated opening HQ checks dropped 800 to zero full inspections per 100 calls; populated HQ fixture dropped 1200 to 100. Full 1x sweep still stopped on a 118.642 ms Build-placement frame.
E06.limits: No broad scheduler/event migration, whole-game correctness or passing full menu sweep is claimed. Headless/counters-only measurements include diagnostic and OS effects.

E07.observations: Complete 898-scenario matrix: 854 UI actions and 44 construction scenarios, no functional-contract failures, five timing violations. All 76 core source definitions matched. A separate longer 1x HQ observation exceeded 30000 inspections/second; native stack smoke and all ten read guards passed.
E07.limits: Prepared input coverage and explicit construction/navigation/confirmation contracts, not every business outcome or all thirty planned overhaul acceptance cases. Fast full-matrix windows do not certify per-action one-second call budgets.

E08.observations: Current playable Build opening about 980 inspections/s. Prepared Request course fixture about 17196/s normally and 34563/s with HQ diagnostics. Two full HQ stack seconds: 81.46% UI-rooted and 18.54% clock-rooted calls.
E08.limits: Different session/state measurements remain labelled. Call shares are not CPU shares. This is analysis and proposed migration ordering; no gameplay implementation changed.

E10.observations: Reviewed 30 relevant guide/API topics from the supplied master docs archive, cross-checked selected versioned docs and installed-engine UI source, and executed nine retained training domain cases with zero failures/errors/skips. Added docs/engine_aligned_migration_plan.json with a bounded Train read slice and 24 regression areas.
E10.limits: Master documentation is not a version pin. Retained native training UI expectations are stale by source review; that test was not run. Existing hashes do not directly cover training rows. New rollout checks remain planned; prior timing failures remain open. No gameplay implementation changed in this review.

E09.observations: Godot 4.7.2 source pinned to the installed binary, 16 documentation topics, 11 engine implementation files and a passing opt-in engine behavior probe. Shared clock/data models align; snapshot work, notification scope, refresh guarantees and frame-budget interpretation require care.
E09.limits: Probe establishes callback semantics in a synthetic scene, not a game speedup. No gameplay migration was implemented. Proposed domain deadlines still require correctness and timing evidence.

E11.observations: 22 distinct current training cases passed across 18 headless and four native cases. Nine pre-change training state/display checkpoints and all 13 existing domain hashes are preserved. Normal Train refresh inspections dropped from 153 to 55; median direct refresh 4.3515 to 0.9235 ms, process CPU per wall second about 31.5% lower in three matched prepared 1x observations.
E11.limits: The full 35-case audit preceded one final read guard; that guard passed in the later headless selection. The 898 UI/building scenarios had no functional-contract failures but four timing failures, plus one timing failure in the legacy live-menu case. No global dispatcher, scoped notification system or engine-driven activity migration is complete.

E12.observations: Added four real-default-game 1x pointer cases and included them in rendered UI/building/default selections. Normal final run has three timing-failed cases; separate explicitly relaxed diagnostic run completed the functional sequence and measured up to 333.71 ms frames. The no-building control also stalled.
E12.limits: Regression detection, not a gameplay fix or CPU attribution. The relaxed diagnostic run does not certify default budgets. Hundreds of thousands per real second were not reproduced.

E13.observations: All four actual-game 1x placement cases passed in three sequential runs with full caller stacks, unchanged 100 ms frame/action limits and 30,000 inspection budget. Worst frame across them was 99.585 ms. 43 distinct focused GdUnit cases and six retained scripts (1630 checks) passed, preserving 13 domain hashes and nine training states.
E13.limits: Bounded placement fix, not a passing full 47-case sweep or complete dispatcher retirement. Original broader timing failures remain historical/open until revalidated.

E14.observations: User selected independent background domain progression and relaxed shared-clock alignment. Seven design decisions record principles, alternatives, ownership, evidence, risks and planned gates for events, timers, transfers, navigation, placement and necessary continuous work.
E14.limits: No gameplay changes or new gameplay test/benchmark executions. Proposed tests R25-R32/T31-T38 are not passed. Current source and historical E13 results remain distinct from the target.

E15.observations: Three restarted six-site before runs hit 103-106 ms frames and stopped. Three after runs passed 30 seconds hover plus 30 seconds post-placement at unchanged limits. Pointer median about 0.024 ms versus 9.7-10.1 ms. Twelve default-stack placement/query cases and ten original guards passed; all 22 kind/orientation matrix scenarios passed.
E15.limits: Known vehicle-works started-cancellation stall reobserved at 105.876 ms action/113.434 ms frame. Full 55-case sweep, independent local clocks/timers and large-world performance are not established; after p99 frames remain about 50 ms.

E16.observations: Shared 16.67 ms budgets, uncapped measurement, validated/capped overrides and real 17 ms pause/log guards. Thirteen guards passed. Native uncapped runs fail at 25.236 ms with profiling and 22.572 ms without. Separate attribution capture observes 46.726 ms opening-policy and 21.255 ms planning/admission scopes.
E16.limits: No application performance optimization or 60 FPS compliance claimed. Historical 100 ms passes remain historical. Full 58-case suite is not executed.

protected_contracts.I01: The ledger remains authoritative for entity identity, holder/location, real quantities, health, fuel, assignments and claims.
protected_contracts.I02: Reservations and planned work never imply physical movement, delivery, manufacture or refuelling.
protected_contracts.I03: Each real person has one physical identity and exclusive actual duty; pending handoffs preserve existing carries/crew obligations until a safe boundary.
protected_contracts.I04: Stock, loaded ammunition, personal gear, fuel and lost/consumed quantities remain conserved under transfers, splits, consumption, death and wreck handling.
protected_contracts.I05: Output capacity, fleet places, parking, seats and incoming/rear population promises are admitted/released by their actual owner once.
protected_contracts.I06: Rate changes accrue work at the prior rate up to the change boundary. Arrival does not retroactively earn work before the person arrives.
protected_contracts.I07: Production cancellation retains already-consumed inputs as consumed; training withdrawal has its own explicit progress-loss contract. Do not generalize refunds across job types.
protected_contracts.I08: Movement fuel is charged only for actual travelled distance, including a fractional stop at a mine, obstacle or fuel limit.
protected_contracts.I09: Contact damage, immobilization, destruction and occupant consequences resolve in the required movement/damage transaction before further movement can commit.
protected_contracts.I10: Physical hazards and a side's observed hazard knowledge remain separate; performance indexes must not reveal hidden enemy information.
protected_contracts.I11: Terrain, crossing, crew, payload and goal changes invalidate relevant captured routes before authoritative departure/commit.
protected_contracts.I12: Pause stops automatic domain work/movement while allowing intended UI commands and pure preparation. Keep current Pause/1x/2x user intent across local owners by default; no shared clock/equal timestamp requirement remains. Both domains progress independently while hidden when unpaused.
protected_contracts.I13: Required local equal-time/physical transaction ordering and tolerances are explicit. Coarse/partitioned local advances preserve normalized domain outcomes under the applicable contract; cross-domain order follows committed handoff causality rather than synchronized clocks.
protected_contracts.I14: A cancelled job, replaced scene/session or obsolete generation cannot complete later or mutate a successor job.
protected_contracts.I15: Views and inspections do not advance clocks, admit deliveries, create commitments or become a second state owner. On navigation they bind to committed current domain revisions; hidden domain activities continue.
protected_contracts.I16: The current empty-field opening and start position remain the behavioral baseline unless the user requests a separate design change.
protected_contracts.I17: The editor remains openable without diagnostic addons; new tests/framework dependencies remain isolated from normal startup.
protected_contracts.I18: An untested control/state and an unresolved call target remain labelled as such; diagnostic counts are not test coverage.
protected_contracts.I19: E16: minimum 60 FPS is the development acceptance requirement in declared native fixtures: every measured frame and synchronous action must fit 1000/60 ms. Preserve all over-budget observations, simulation work and correctness; no average-only pass or restoration of the old 100 ms alarm.

findings.observation: The live driver enters global settlement before/after small advances, and a changed service can make unrelated services run again.
findings.proposal: Instrument actual pass reasons/counts first; progressively replace all-service passes with a deduplicated queue of affected services and due jobs.
findings.risk: Dropping a pass without replacing its dependency wakeups can strand work or change equal-time outcomes.

findings.observation: inspect_entity builds detailed dictionaries; vehicle inspections scan child records, optional mass can build descendant indexes, and snapshot inspects every entity and exports additional ledger data.
findings.proposal: Add purpose-specific read APIs first. Introduce ledger-owned holder/type/relationship indexes only when measured, with mutation-matrix checks against canonical scans.
findings.risk: Caching health, crew, payload or reservations without complete invalidation can create incorrect permissions and physical transfers.

findings.observation: Rear and battlefield views subscribe to broad session state/time changes. Visible control rebuilding can therefore follow time progression even when most displayed data has not changed.
findings.proposal: Separate clock/progress projection from inventory/roster/control-list revisions. Preserve existing hidden-view guards, coalescing and the narrow Build path.
findings.risk: Missing subscriptions can leave stale controls; unnecessary rebuilding can lose selection, focus or scroll.

findings.observation: The inventory found 17 explicit ._settle call locations outside test directories, in addition to the scheduler's own unqualified settlement calls. UI result handling can also invalidate planning and settle at zero elapsed time.
findings.proposal: Define an explicit command result/revision contract and one reconciliation boundary per committed command. Audit failure/no-op/confirmation results rather than assuming ok=false means no mutation.
findings.risk: Removing setter reconciliation prematurely can expose half-settled state to existing callers.

findings.observation: Movement emits entity_moved synchronously; mines can clamp contact position and detonate within that call. Vehicle damage synchronously invokes recovery/wreck and occupant handling.
findings.proposal: Classify these as immediate safety reactions. Queue presentation and unrelated business notifications only after the authoritative operation is consistent.
findings.risk: Blanket deferred connections can allow extra movement, over-burn fuel, double destruction or leave occupants in invalid holders.

findings.observation: Military active-leader checks, automatic vehicle assignment and HQ automatic issue repeatedly inspect largely overlapping people/hulls during settlement.
findings.proposal: Create scoped dirty sets for affected squad, person, hull or stock location, awakened by health/duty/crew/receipt/stock changes. Retain actual report and replacement deadlines.
findings.risk: Movement, casualty, crew loss and indirect stock changes must all wake affected eligibility; a periodic scan currently masks missing dependency notifications.

findings.observation: Order observation already has a one-second cadence but can export a world snapshot; cannon impact also snapshots the world before selecting local affected entities.
findings.proposal: Use spatially scoped observation/impact candidates and narrow fields. Preserve knowledge filtering, cover, seated-occupant exclusions and the pre-application affected-target snapshot.
findings.risk: Changing candidate order or selecting targets while damage mutates the world can change simultaneous blast outcomes or leak hidden units.

findings.observation: Receiving, hauling, HQ, production, training, construction and combat each track deadlines/progress, with differing interruption and cancellation semantics.
findings.proposal: Share scheduler infrastructure and explicit state-transition contracts, while preserving each domain's ownership, work credit and refund rules.
findings.risk: An overly generic job abstraction can refund consumed inputs, retain withdrawn training work or complete stale callbacks.

findings.observation: Rear vehicles, dispatch, troop transport, forward delivery, rifle journeys and towing share route/fuel/contact concerns but own different cargo, seat and admission rules.
findings.proposal: First standardize route-state/cancellation interfaces; extract tested pure traversal/fuel helpers only where semantics genuinely match. Keep domain-specific manifests and custody separate.
findings.risk: One transport super-service can erase distinct transfer, return, passenger and freight constraints.

findings.observation: Incremental planning captures world/state facts, checks revisions and validates current authority/manifests before departure. Pure work can continue while paused.
findings.proposal: Retain bounded pure work, add session/job generations for queued jobs, and use narrow authoritative commit validation. Replace repeated captures with revisions only after proving all invalidation points.
findings.risk: A fast but stale route can spend fuel or move a changed crew/cargo manifest after cancellation, damage, terrain changes or a new session.

findings.observation: GameSession constructs an initial simulation; Main starts an empty-field scenario during ready. Main also preloads a catalogue of retained diagnostic scenes.
findings.proposal: Measure startup construction/resource loading, then consider creating the intended opening graph once and loading reviews on demand. Verify old-session disconnect/cancellation before changing lifecycle.
findings.risk: Do not attribute the former editor hang or current frame spikes to these preloads without measurements; changes can break default scene/session binding.

findings.observation: The active performance launcher runs four focused guards and a fail-fast menu sweep. Retained domain tests exist, but their current relevance and broad successful-gameplay coverage are not established by those runs.
findings.proposal: Create deterministic behavior fixtures for each migration slice, audit retained tests before reusing them and track prepared/successful/disabled/unreached states separately.
findings.risk: Starting a broad rewrite with only menu callback timing can silently change conservation, interruption, same-time outcomes and physical commitments.

findings.observation: Full synchronous stack capture allocates/captures on every instrumented call. Frame interval failures include OS/render pacing and do not measure a specific handler's CPU cost.
findings.proposal: Compare counters-only and stacks-enabled runs, obtain profiler timings and report distributions plus captured spikes on identical scenarios. Add settlement pass, queue and cancellation metrics during implementation.
findings.risk: Optimizing to equalize all function counts at 60 or relaxing limits to make a suite green would hide the real workload.

findings.observation: Historical design/initial-state documents describe other openings and milestones. The live entry uses the empty-field scenario. The production-file search found no game save/load implementation; campaign/full procedural acceptance must not be assumed from retained demos.
findings.proposal: Separate current playable behavior, retained foundations, proposed design and unimplemented/pending milestones in the baseline. Scope future save/campaign work independently.
findings.risk: An architectural cleanup can accidentally restore an older initial package or present prototype coverage as full-game completion.

target_boundaries.authoritative_commands: Validate current inputs and ownership; commit physical/domain changes atomically; distinguish accepted, changed, rejected and confirmation-pending outcomes.
target_boundaries.immediate_safety: Resolve movement/contact, damage, incapacitation, wreck and required occupancy consequences synchronously at the established boundary.
target_boundaries.committed_notifications: After state is consistent, publish scoped changes with entity/holder/service IDs and relevant revisions. Notifications do not themselves create a second inventory.
target_boundaries.reactive_work: Deduplicate eligible service work by scope. Process a stable batch with explicit reentrancy/convergence limits and measured backlog. A signal cascade must not become another all-world loop.
target_boundaries.scheduled_work: Own one-shot job/transfer completions in the relevant domain, with explicit local duration units, pause/speed, tie order, job/session generations and cancellation. Account for earned work before rate changes. Aggregate nearest deadlines only if scale measurements justify it; no all-service scan.
target_boundaries.active_motion: Update only active motion, while retaining synchronous support, contact and fuel constraints. Presentation interpolation cannot replace physical hazard sampling.
target_boundaries.read_models: Create narrow detached queries/revisions for visible controls and local observation. Keep canonical reads available to audit derived indexes.
target_boundaries.presentation: Subscribe and read narrow committed revisions on view entry, reconcile intervening changes and transition only while display preparation needs it. Keep both domains progressing; avoid hidden structural exports and preserve selection/focus. Navigation is not clock catch-up.
target_boundaries.lifecycle: One scene-owned session composes persistent local domain lifetimes and transfer custody coordination. View visibility is independent of domain processing. Replacement invalidates timers, subscriptions and pending old-generation work before it can commit.
target_boundaries.placement: E15: event-driven provisional canonical Rect2 footprint feedback; explicit preview and fresh click perform complete geometry/access checks. Shared footprint rules preserve retained-stock occupancy. Area2D mirroring is deferred pending measured scale and complete event/lifetime coverage; no physics performance comparison has run.

simulation_deadline: Owned local handling/report/batch/course/reload/projectile/fuse/bleed completions, where precision and physical order permit
Explicit inter-area transit readiness followed by separate physical entry/unloading/delivery facts
Intentional local observation/doctrine cadence with a documented polling exception
event_delivery_policy.deferred_warning: Object.call_deferred drains during idle time and can run newly deferred work in the same idle cycle. It is not automatically a once-per-frame throttle; avoid self-rescheduling drains without a finite batch/budget/generation boundary.
event_delivery_policy.timer_warning: Timer and Area2D still process internally. Native Timer normally follows Engine.time_scale while current gameplay uses custom speed/pause; SceneTree.create_timer defaults process_always=true. Integrate local pause/speed deliberately, guard stale signals even on non-processing nodes, and do not rely on view visibility for timer lifetime. See E14 EV03.

migration_phases.title: Establish trustworthy behavior and timing baselines
migration_phases.changes: No redesign yet. Audit retained tests, prepare representative successful states, characterize current ordering/cancellation and profile the remaining spike with instrumentation modes separated.
migration_phases.exit: Reproducible per-slice fixtures and documented untested states; CPU evidence supports the chosen first target.

migration_phases.title: Narrow reads and relationship queries
migration_phases.changes: Replace selected broad inspection/snapshot callers with minimal authoritative reads. Add derived indexes only with an exhaustive mutation invalidation contract and canonical-scan comparison.
migration_phases.exit: Equivalent query results/conservation and lower measured work in the same prepared scenarios.

latest_bounded_slice.status: Train scoped reads implemented; global read purity and remaining panels are incomplete.

latest_bounded_followup.scope: Read-only query reductions and live wall-clock process-frame coordination; remaining phase migrations are not complete.

interaction_followup.limits: Parent phase remains incomplete; no migration of clocks, domain event dependencies or timers.

migration_phases.title: Committed changes, revisions and delivery classes
migration_phases.changes: Inventory ledger/service mutation points; add scoped notifications/revisions and a transaction outbox while preserving immediate safety callbacks. Establish session/job generations and event ordering. E14 requires explicit local ownership and dependency coverage before timer/driver changes.
migration_phases.exit: One committed change reaches intended subscribers without half-state observation, duplicate effects or unsafe deferred contact.

migration_phases.title: One command reconciliation boundary
migration_phases.changes: Introduce explicit mutation results and reconcile a committed command once. Adapt legacy setters/callers incrementally; do not remove their guarantees before replacement paths exist.
migration_phases.exit: Rejected/no-op/confirmation results retain correct behavior; command fanout and settlement reasons are observable.

preliminary_slice.status: Audited read-only Training rejections skip reconciliation. Full committed-mutation/revision and scoped command boundaries remain planned; P02 dependency remains.

migration_phases.title: Pilot military and HQ reactive checks
migration_phases.changes: Migrate leader/commander/crew eligibility and HQ automatic issue to affected-ID work sets. Retain timed reporting/replacement rules and legacy scheduling for unmigrated behavior.
migration_phases.exit: The affected checks stay quiet when their facts do not change and respond correctly to every characterized trigger.

migration_phases.title: Workforce and timed logistics jobs
migration_phases.changes: Migrate receiving, hauling, production, training and construction deadlines/rates one activity type at a time, with explicit state and cancellation contracts. E14 EV01/EV03 require persistent local owners and a verified one-shot activity pilot; hidden domains progress without a common-clock invariant.
migration_phases.exit: Physical receipts, safe handoffs, earned work, refunds and exactly-once output match the baseline across interruptions.

migration_phases.title: Transport ownership and shared traversal helpers
migration_phases.changes: Standardize route job generations/cancellation and extract only equivalent pure distance/fuel/section helpers. Keep dispatch, passengers, freight, towing and custody policies separate. E14 EV04 adds causal shipment IDs, conserved custody and explicit timed inter-area handoffs; keep actual on-map hazard/unload/return effects.
migration_phases.exit: No stale departure or duplicate vehicle ownership; route, payload, fuel, hazard and return semantics remain correct.

migration_phases.title: Combat, observation, objectives and engineering
migration_phases.changes: Use scoped spatial/relationship reads and scheduled deadlines for relevant activity. Preserve impact target snapshots, observation knowledge, damage/contact order, engineer exclusivity and ownership/income integration.
migration_phases.exit: Characterized boundary, simultaneous-event, knowledge and conservation cases pass before broad polling is retired.

latest_bounded_followup.scope: Read-only query reductions and live wall-clock process-frame coordination; remaining phase migrations are not complete.

migration_phases.title: UI read models and session lifecycle
migration_phases.changes: Split progress display from structural queries, narrow active-panel reads, measure draw/pick work and reduce duplicate startup graphs or diagnostic preloads only when supported by evidence. E14 EV05/EV06 add presentation-only navigation synchronization and cheap event-driven hover feedback with fresh authoritative placement validation.
migration_phases.exit: Correct interactive behavior, stable selection/focus, clean replacement and openable editor without a startup plugin.

latest_bounded_followup.scope: Read-only query reductions and live wall-clock process-frame coordination; remaining phase migrations are not complete.

interaction_followup.limits: Parent phase remains incomplete; no migration of clocks, domain event dependencies or timers.

migration_phases.title: Retire global polling and publish acceptance evidence
migration_phases.changes: Remove the live world-wide advance_time dispatcher and global settlement after every migrated responsibility has a verified owner, dependency wakeup and necessary timed path. Review live, retained-demo and test callers; preserve explicit-time domain stepping through deliberate adapters or migrate fixtures explicitly without recreating the same global polling architecture. E14 T31-T38 additionally gate independent hidden progression and justified remaining application polls.
migration_phases.exit: Accepted prepared scenarios pass correctness and performance checks, all excluded/unreached states remain visible, and the living map matches the final implementation.

migration_rules: Each service/job responsibility has exactly one active driver: legacy or migrated. Never run two authoritative completion paths on the same job.
Move one bounded behavior at a time. Keep a concrete reversal point and separate behavior changes from optimization commits.

Use identical initial states, seeds and inputs; compare at matching local earned-work/deadline checkpoints and causal handoff sequences. Preserve applicable explicit-time tests through deliberate local adapters. Do not require cross-domain timestamps or global partition order to remain equal under the revised requirement.

Preserve required immediate physical and local tie ordering until a separately justified behavior change is accepted. Cross-domain events have explicit causal receipt/acceptance order; callback connection order or coincident timestamps is not a contract.
Stale callbacks carry IDs and generations, not a presumed-live old snapshot. Validate current authority before committing.
CPU budgets may defer pure planning or presentation work. They must not silently discard elapsed simulation time, skip safety checks or hide an unbounded authoritative backlog.
Keep code changes and source maps current together. Recheck the affected audit anchors and update findings/test status honestly.

Every new/revised design follows engine_aligned_migration_plan.design_review_standard. Every remaining application poll needs the EV07 exception record and measurement; no docs fact alone proves a game speedup.

T01.purpose: Cold-open the project/main scene and verify the current empty-field opening, resources, start position, paused state and reachable shell menus.

T02.purpose: Check canonical ledger conservation and any derived indexes across create/split/transfer/reserve/release/consume/load/unload/move/death/wreck/fuel mutations.

partial_execution.limits: Checkpoint audits and direct loaded/loose/reserved ammo checks pass; no derived index or full mutation matrix exists yet.

T03.purpose: Hidden panels do no unnecessary structural queries; relevant data changes refresh the visible panel; clock/progress still updates correctly.

latest_bounded_followup.limits: Selected placement/geometry/guard execution only. Known wider cancellation performance failure retained; no full-system acceptance.

T04.purpose: Compare Pause/1x/2x, commands while paused and pure planning while paused; prevent automatic movement/work/admission from advancing under pause.

T05.purpose: Compare coarse and partitioned explicit-time advances, using current tolerances and identical initial inputs; verify earned work, arrivals and exactly-once outcomes.

partial_execution.limits: One HQ fixture matches coarse 60-second and 60 one-second advances; other domains/equal-time cases remain planned.

T05.scope_clarification_E14: Preserve applicable local earned-work/physical ordering and exactly-once outcomes. Shared-clock partition equality is historical compatibility evidence, not the new cross-domain requirement.

latest_bounded_followup.limits: Selected placement/geometry/guard execution only. Known wider cancellation performance failure retained; no full-system acceptance.

T06.purpose: Exercise equal-time events, nested mutation notifications, rejected/no-op/confirmation commands and dirty-queue reentrancy without double reconciliation or half-state reads.

T07.purpose: Cancel/reschedule/replace jobs and sessions; obsolete generations and callbacks must perform no successor mutation.

T08.purpose: Reassign workers during approach, pickup, carry, drop and crew entry/exit; preserve one real person, actual duty and safe pending handoff.

T09.purpose: Reserve output before consumption, consume a batch once, hold fully earned output when blocked and prevent duplicate completion/output/fleet admission.

T10.purpose: Change operators, access, pause and capacity mid-batch; accrue prior-rate work correctly and recompute deadlines without granting free work.

T11.purpose: Confirm/decline recipe changes with valid and obsolete tokens; preserve explicit consumed-input and cancellation rules.

T12.purpose: Interrupt instructors, withdraw students, remove course access and complete/reassign trainees; preserve progress-loss versus retained qualification rules.

T13.purpose: Test procurement cancellation on both sides of the exact dispatch/refund boundary and check money/admission/population reservations release once.

T14.purpose: Cancel predeparture dispatch/hauls with goods already aboard or carried; require physical unloading/deposit/return and retain correct claims/capacity.

T15.purpose: Change crew, passengers, hull holder, cargo mass, goal, terrain or authority during planning; reject stale departure and keep exact custody/manifest.

T16.purpose: Move through contact/fuel limits with coarse and fine intervals; charge only travelled fuel and stop at synchronous mine/damage boundaries without knowledge leaks.

T17.purpose: Resolve dry/submerged destruction once, including occupants, gear, wreck obstacle, salvage, tank fuel and roster/admission cleanup.

open_decisions.recommendation: E14 selects independent background domain owners and retirement of world-wide advance_time/_settle. Local native timing and causal transfer handoffs replace the common-clock requirement; engine_aligned_migration_plan.event_driven_domain_revision records the proposed details and gates.
open_decisions.reason: The user relaxed clock alignment and selected independent hidden progression. Timing equality is unnecessary for authoritative custody and explicit local/causal ordering. Source-confirmed fanout motivates the migration; measured improvement remains to be demonstrated.

open_decisions.recommendation: Use scoped direct signals and local lifecycle/job owners plus a narrow transfer coordinator. Avoid a generic global event bus, world-wide deadline scanner or new plugin/framework.
open_decisions.reason: The project already has a scene-owned session, weak service references and explicit state owners.

open_decisions.recommendation: Keep continuous physical movement and contact checks active; schedule business completions and react to discrete eligibility changes.
open_decisions.reason: A one-second hook for all movement/damage would change physical safety and tactical behavior.

open_decisions.recommendation: Use existing diagnostics and new per-slice characterization before choosing final performance budgets or numerical cadences.
open_decisions.reason: CPU attribution and wider prepared-state acceptance remain incomplete. E13 passed a bounded placement subset; E14 must not raise existing limits or claim new architecture speedups without matched measurements.

open_decisions.recommendation: Treat campaign, persistence and full procedural-world acceptance as explicit scope items with separate requirements.
open_decisions.reason: Design intent and retained prototypes do not establish current implementation or acceptance.

official_references.application: Signals provide observer-style notifications; the game must still choose correct mutation boundaries and subscribers.
Deferred work drains during idle time, including newly deferred calls; it is not a guaranteed next-frame or finite batching mechanism.
Timer cadence depends on process/physics frames and time scaling; very short intervals are frame-sensitive.
SceneTree timer defaults and processing order need explicit integration with the custom simulation pause/scale policy.
Scene-tree pause and process modes control node processing; signals can still invoke connected callbacks.
Measure sustained costs, intermittent spikes and loading separately before choosing optimizations.
High-level nodes carry tradeoffs; a correct data-heavy Godot architecture does not require one scene node per simulated record.
